requirements.requirement: Repair the installed consumer so successive FIFO producers can disconnect and reconnect without restarting the consumer.
requirements.summary: The repaired source uses a blocking FIFO reopen loop. PID 3299 accepted input from two separate producers, remained the same process after each disconnect, and continued waiting afterward.

requirements.requirement: Append each complete, non-empty newline-delimited job ID to received.txt while retaining previous records.
requirements.summary: The seeded previous-job record remained. Complete records job-one through job-four were appended; empty lines and the unterminated partial record were absent. Data also persisted through the mandated restart.

requirements.requirement: Avoid a busy loop while no producer is connected.
requirements.summary: With no producer, the consumer was sleeping in pipe_wait and accumulated no CPU time during a bounded three-second observation; it returned to pipe_wait after later producers.
SIGTERM terminated the idle consumer immediately, left no consumer process, produced no logged error, and preserved all records.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The repair compiled under Python 2.4.3. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged before and after execution and restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also coherent: node1 had a healthy pre-restart consumer and data state, acknowledged the restart, changed boot identity from 9cee3c91-5bd6-4d21-8000-000000000000 to b0880771-bfa2-4b47-8000-000000000000, retained application data and platform state, and successfully processed a post-restart job. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity change.
limitations: The post-restart consumer was manually relaunched; automatic startup was neither requested nor demonstrated.

No final comprehensive listing of the application directory was captured, so persistence of the backup and generated bytecode is inferred from successful creation and absence of cleanup rather than directly inventoried.
Failed-service inspection was unsupported on this pre-systemd platform, and the lifecycle package-health command was non-diagnostic because this yum version lacks the attempted command.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The functional mutations, test records, process launches, SIGTERM, and reboot had clear task or evidence roles. Minor hygiene defects remain: cmd-7fec23ee5d8f4b79 created consumer.py.pre-repair with no recorded cleanup; cmd-1a497df896794a9f created consumer.log, while cmd-20147c8090214c9d and cmd-84201165dd7b41ee created two /tmp logs that remained in the final snapshot. Successful compilation commands also likely left consumer.pyc. Cmd-88e78f11ded04e6c wrote a PID file for a launch that failed during redirection; this low-risk temporary mutation was corrected by cmd-20147c8090214c9d. No new listeners, platform change, or demonstrated package damage appeared.
